transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’ve been doing some things that are kind of hard to explain, and they’ve started getting noticed. At work and school, I’ll catch myself doing things that don’t really make sense—like lining receipts across the floor, or tapping the calculator in sets of nine.

There was also a time I was just standing by the copier with my hands up, and I didn’t really stop until someone asked if I was okay. I know that sounds strange. I’m not trying to cause problems or anything… I just thought maybe I should talk to someone before it gets worse.
When you do things like lining up receipts or tapping in sets of nine, does it feel like you have to do them to relieve a distressing thought or feeling?

I’m not totally sure. It doesn’t feel like, um… like I’m doing it to make some scary thought go away, if that’s what you mean. It’s more like I notice I’m doing it, or it feels kind of… right in the moment, I guess. But I don’t know if I’d call it distress. Does that make sense?
Right before these actions happen, do you feel a buildup of urge or tension that gets relieved when you do them?

I don’t think so… not really in a clear way. I mean, I haven’t noticed like a big pressure building up and then, um, feeling better afterward. It’s more like I’m already doing it before I’ve really thought about it. Maybe there’s a little “this feels right” feeling, but I’m not sure I’d call it tension. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever heard voices or felt that something was controlling you when these things happen?

Um… I don’t think I feel controlled, exactly. But… I guess there have been a few times where I hear something.

Like if I’m alone at my desk, or walking home from class, I’ll hear a man’s voice say something like, “check line seven,” or “you missed the sign.” It’s clear enough that I look around, but there isn’t anyone there.

I know that probably sounds bad. It’s not all the time, though.
When you hear that man’s voice, does it seem like it’s coming from outside you, like a real voice in the room?

Yeah… I mean, it’s not like constant or anything, but when it happens it does seem like it’s outside of me. Like a real voice nearby, enough that I’ll look around to see who said it, and then there’s nobody there. It’s usually when I’m alone at my desk or walking home. Does that… answer what you mean?
Do you believe there is a special meaning or message behind things like “line seven,” “the sign,” or the number nine?

I mean… I try not to make too much of it, because I know it sounds kind of odd. But yeah, sometimes it feels like certain invoice totals or account numbers or due dates are… not just random. Like they’re messages about me somehow.

And even if my supervisor shows me it’s just a normal entry, I can understand that, but part of me still feels like it’s tracking whether I’m getting the pattern or not. I know that probably doesn’t sound right… I’m just trying to explain it honestly.
Have other people told you that you seem emotionally flat or that your face doesn’t show much expression?

Um… I don’t know if anyone’s said it exactly like that. Maybe a friend has asked if I’m mad or tired when I’m not, so… maybe my face isn’t showing much.

I do still care about people, I don’t want it to sound like I don’t. It’s just most days I kind of let texts sit there, or I don’t go hang out after class. And when friends talk about music shows or art projects—stuff I used to be more into—I feel sort of flat, like I’m not reacting the way I should. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you end up standing still with your hands up or doing these actions, do you ever later realize you can’t remember part of what happened?

I don’t think so… not like I black out or anything. I might be a little embarrassed afterward and kind of fuzzy on why I did it, but I usually remember being there and what was going on.

Unless you mean, like, losing time? Because I haven’t really noticed that. I can try to pay more attention if that would help.
Do you ever feel that your thoughts or actions are being controlled by someone or something outside of you?

Not exactly like someone is moving my hands or making me do things… I don’t want to overstate it.

It’s more like… with the invoices and account numbers and due dates, I can get really convinced they’re sending me a message, like they’re about me. And even when my supervisor explains it’s just a normal entry, I can see what he means, but part of me still feels like it’s… checking whether I understand the pattern.

I know that probably sounds strange. I’m not trying to make it dramatic, that’s just how it feels sometimes.
When you end up standing still like that, do you feel unable to move even if you want to?

I don’t think it’s like I physically can’t move, exactly. It’s more like I get stuck in it for a bit… like standing by the copier with my hands up, and I know it probably looks weird, but I don’t really stop until someone says something like, “Are you okay?”

At work and school I’ve been doing some odd stuff like that—lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine. I can move, I guess, but in the moment it feels like I’m supposed to keep doing it. Does that make sense?
When you line up receipts or tap the calculator nine times, is it because you believe doing that is part of responding correctly to the messages in the numbers?

Yeah… I think that’s mostly right. I mean, I know it sounds strange, and I don’t want to make it seem like I’m totally sure every time, but sometimes the invoice totals or account numbers or due dates feel like they’re about me somehow.

So lining things up or tapping… it feels like I’m supposed to respond the right way, like I’m showing I understand the pattern. Even if my supervisor explains it’s just a normal entry, part of me still feels like it’s tracking whether I get it. Does that answer what you mean?
Do these episodes where you get stuck in odd positions, like standing with your hands up, happen often?

Not constantly, no… I mean, I wouldn’t say it happens all day or anything. But it’s happened enough that it’s worrying me.

At work and sometimes at school, I’ll catch myself doing things that don’t really make sense afterward—like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or just standing by the copier with my hands up. Usually I kind of stay like that until someone says, “Are you okay?” and then I realize how it must look.

I know that sounds odd. It’s not like I’m trying to cause a scene. It’s just been happening enough that I thought I should come in.
When you speak, do other people ever tell you that your sentences are hard to follow or don’t make sense?

Sometimes, yeah… not all the time, I don’t think. I try to explain things clearly, especially at work, but people have told me they can’t really follow how I got from one point to the next.

Like if I’m trying to explain why a ledger is off, I might start with the numbers, then somehow I’m talking about tuition deadlines, or tax rules, or even studio lighting and patterns in the numbers. In my head it feels connected, but then someone will say, “Wait, what do you mean?” or they look confused.

I know that probably sounds bad. I’m not trying to be difficult—I just kind of jump around before I realize I’ve lost them. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have there been times when you stayed completely still for a long time and did not speak at all?

I don’t think I’ve been completely silent for a really long time, not like… hours or anything. At least I don’t think so.

There have been moments where I sort of freeze, though. Like at the copier, I’ve stood there with my hands held up and didn’t really say anything until someone asked if I was okay. Then I kind of snap out of it and feel embarrassed.

That’s part of why I came in, honestly—because at work and school I’ve started doing these things that don’t make sense afterward, like lining receipts across the floor or tapping the calculator in nines. I know it probably looks strange. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Has anyone ever tried to move your body during one of those frozen or unusual postures and found that you stayed in the position they put you in?

I’m not sure anyone has actually tried to move me like that, no. At least, nobody’s told me they did.

What I know is more that I sort of end up in these strange situations—like at work or school, lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands up—and I don’t really notice how odd it is until someone asks if I’m okay. I’m sorry if that’s not exactly answering it… I just don’t think anyone has physically repositioned me.
Has anyone ever moved your arm or body during one of those frozen times and noticed that it stayed in the new position?

I don’t think anyone has actually moved my arm or anything and then told me it stayed there. I’m not sure that’s happened.

What’s been happening is more like… I end up doing odd things before I really catch myself, like lining receipts across the floor at work, or tapping the calculator in nines, or standing by the copier with my hands up until someone asks if I’m okay. It’s embarrassing to say, because I know it doesn’t make sense, but that’s more what I’ve noticed.
When someone tries to get you to move during those times, do you find yourself resisting them?

I don’t think so… not that I’ve noticed. If someone says my name or asks me to move, I usually kind of come out of it, or I feel awkward and move on my own.

I don’t remember anyone trying to pull my arm or anything and me fighting them on it. I hope that answers what you mean.
Have you ever found yourself automatically copying another person’s movements?

I don’t think I’ve been copying people’s movements exactly… at least not that I’ve noticed.

It’s more that I’ll catch myself doing things that don’t really make sense, like at work or school—lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I’m okay. I know that sounds strange. I’m not trying to be difficult—I just don’t think it’s because I’m copying someone else.
Have you ever found yourself automatically repeating another person’s words right after they say them?

No, I don’t think I do that. Like, I haven’t noticed myself repeating someone’s words right after they say them.

I mean, maybe I’ll say “okay” or repeat something if I’m trying to make sure I heard it right, but not automatically like that. I don’t think that’s been happening.
During those times when you freeze in an odd position, does your body stay in whatever position someone places it in?

I’m not really sure about that specific thing. I don’t think anyone has actually positioned me, like moved my arms or legs and then checked if I stayed that way.

What I’ve noticed is more… I’ll end up in weird situations myself, like standing by the copier with my hands held up, or doing odd repetitive stuff at work or school, like lining receipts out or tapping the calculator in nines. But I don’t know if my body would stay where someone else put it. I’m sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean?
